sources: https://www.ksoutdoors.gov/about-kdwp/where-we-work/state-fishing-lakes/douglas-state-fishing-lake - the live page answers 403 to plain HTTP; read the Wayback capture of 2026-07-12 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260712030308/https://www.ksoutdoors.gov/about-kdwp/where-we-work/state-fishing-lakes/douglas-state-fishing-lake) on 2026-11-06: 'The 538-acre Wildlife Area surrounding Douglas State Fishing Lake is primarily timbered'; 'Primitive camping areas, four vault restrooms, and picnic tables are provided for area users. Camping is only allowed in provided areas. Please carry out all garbage.'; 'Motorized boating allowed for hunting and fishing purposes only'; 'Camping and campfires in designated areas only'; 'Campfires in provided metal rings only'; 'Target shooting, off-road vehicle use, and horse riding are prohibited'; 'Special Features: Handicapped accessible fishing dock'; Public Lands Manager '(785) 887-6882'; no facility coordinates

KDWP camping page, Wayback capture of 2025-10-28 (https://web.archive.org/web/20251028091024/https://ksoutdoors.gov/Services/Outdoor-Activities/Camping); Wayback rate-limited my own fetch on 2026-11-06, so read from the copy of that same capture saved earlier today in batch p3-309: 'All campers and camping units at state fishing lakes or wildlife areas are limited to designated camping areas and a stay of not more than seven consecutive days ...'; 'Not all state fishing lakes and wildlife areas allow camping. For those that do, there is currently no cost to camp, but camping first-come, first served and reservations are not accepted.'

K.A.R. 115-8-9 as amended April 2023, Kansas Register Vol. 42 No. 14 (https://kssos.org/publications/Register/Volume-42/Issues/Issue-14/04-06-23-51015.html), read 2026-11-06: '(a) Camping shall be allowed only in designated areas on department lands and waters ...'; '(c) All campers and camping units at a state fishing lake or wildlife area shall be limited to a stay of not more than seven consecutive days on that department managed land unless otherwise established by posted notice or authorized by written permit from the department. Upon completing seven consecutive days on the same campsite, each person and all property of each person shall be absent from the department-managed area for at least five days.'

fees.source: KDWP camping page (Wayback 2025-10-28): 'For those that do, there is currently no cost to camp'; the Douglas page (Wayback 2026-07-12) lists no fee. Read 2026-11-06

values.note: Free, first come; no reservations at Kansas state fishing lakes. Seven consecutive days at a state fishing lake, then five days away (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), amended 2023); a longer stay needs a written KDWP permit.

booking.source: KDWP camping page (Wayback 2025-10-28): 'camping first-come, first served and reservations are not accepted', 'a stay of not more than seven consecutive days'; K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), Kansas Register 2023-04-06; the Douglas page posts no different limit. Read 2026-11-06

facilities.source: KDWP Douglas page (Wayback 2026-07-12): 'four vault restrooms'. Read 2026-11-06

note: KDWP state fishing lake in timbered hills between Baldwin City and Lawrence, with a 538-acre wildlife area. Primitive camping in the designated areas only, with picnic tables, fire rings and four vault toilets. Boats for fishing and hunting only; no horses or off-road vehicles. --Claude
summary: KDWP Douglas page (Wayback 2026-07-12): primitive camping areas, four vault restrooms, designated areas only; free and FCFS; max 7 nights (new). Camping areas not located on any page I could read, so waterfront and pin left as stored. Phone missing -> (785) 887-6882.
flags: WATERFRONT: stored 'not waterfront' left alone, unconfirmed. KDWP gives no location for the camping areas (the 'Douglas SFL & WA' brochure that may map them stayed unread). On Esri the gravel areas are all at the water: a big gravel lot and boat ramp at the east end of the dam (38.8030,-95.1553) and four or five gravel pull-off loops with docks along the west-shore road (around 38.800-38.804,-95.164), each 5-30 m from the lake on open ground. If any of those is a camping area this would be LAKEVIEW or LAKEFRONT, but I can't tell camping from fishing-access parking from the air.

PIN 38.80416,-95.15504 is in woods ~90 m north of the east-end gravel lot and ramp (no visible camping there); Google's 38.79974,-95.15754 is in the lake. Not moved - no camping area located to move it to. Worth a look by whoever reads the brochure.
